subject: Replace genotypes instead of clone correct

messages.author: ae97acd9e10a650f
messages.subject: Replace genotypes instead of clone correct
parts:
Hello!

I am looking to define clonal lineages in my data (using mlg.filter), and force all of the members of the cloanal lineages to have the exact same genotype.  In other words, instead of clone correct my data, I would like to replace the genotypes that would be removed by clonecorrect with the single representative genotype that would remain in the clone corrected dataset.  In this way, I will retain the original number of samples and sampling locations.  Is there a way to do this in poppr, or do I have to do this manually? 

The reason I want to do this is because I am using k-means to define clusters in my data (find.clusters in adegenet).  When I use a clone corrected dataset, I can easily choose the optimal number of clusters.  However, when I use the dataset after mlg.filter (clones are defined but all samples are still there), that same number of clusters is no longer appropriate, and in fact, I see that there isn't an optimal number of clusters - more is always better.  Since find.clusters and dapc accept genind objects and ignore the mlg slot of my genclone object, I am assuming this means the genotypes of my clones are "very" different, because if they were the same, I should get the same number of clusters with more samples are in those clusters. 

Thanks,
Sandra

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Replace genotypes instead of clone correct
parts:
Hi Sandra,

Thank you for posting this question here. See my answers below.

Hello!

I am looking to define clonal lineages in my data (using mlg.filter), and force all of the members of the cloanal lineages to have the exact same genotype.  In other words, instead of clone correct my data, I would like to replace the genotypes that would be removed by clonecorrect with the single representative genotype that would remain in the clone corrected dataset.  In this way, I will retain the original number of samples and sampling locations.  Is there a way to do this in poppr, or do I have to do this manually?

My recommendation: never manually (read: cut and paste) data manually. This leads to error down the line. There is no elegant way to do this automatically in poppr, but I've placed an example of how you can do this here: https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/bacbad22c27251196829052652b985c8. Basically, you use mlg.id() to get individuals by MLG, create a data frame from the genclone object, replace the genotypes in the data frame, and then convert back to a genclone object.

The reason I want to do this is because I am using k-means to define clusters in my data (find.clusters in adegenet).  When I use a clone corrected dataset, I can easily choose the optimal number of clusters.  However, when I use the dataset after mlg.filter (clones are defined but all samples are still there), that same number of clusters is no longer appropriate, and in fact, I see that there isn't an optimal number of clusters - more is always better.  Since find.clusters and dapc accept genind objects and ignore the mlg slot of my genclone object, I am assuming this means the genotypes of my clones are "very" different, because if they were the same, I should get the same number of clusters with more samples are in those clusters.

The difference between your clusters is dependent on the distance used and the clustering algorithm. By default, the clustering algorithm is "farthest neighbor", which does not allow individuals to be in the same cluster if the specified distance is exceeded.

It should be noted that there is a random component to find.clusters(), so you want to make sure that you adjust parameters like n.start in to ensure you find convergence within the same data set.

Best,
Zhian
